question: A 4×3×10 rectangular prism supports a half-cylinder of radius 2 and length 10, with no overlap. Find the combined volume.
solution: Prism V=4·3·10=120. Half-cylinder V=(1/2)π·2²·10=20π. Add to obtain 120+20π.

question: A triangular prism has a triangular base with base 6 ft and altitude 4 ft, and length 7 ft. It is joined to a 6×2×7 rectangular prism without overlap. Find the total volume.
solution: Triangular base area=(1/2)·6·4=12; triangular-prism volume=12·7=84. Rectangular volume=6·2·7=84. Total=168 ft³.

question: A hemisphere of radius 3 cm caps a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. Find their combined volume.
solution: Hemisphere V=(2/3)π·3³=18π. Cylinder V=π·3²·5=45π. Combined=63π cm³.

question: A cube with side length 6 in has a cylindrical hole of radius 1 in drilled completely through its height. Find the remaining volume.
solution: Cube volume=6³=216. Removed cylinder volume=π·1²·6=6π. Subtract: 216−6π in³.

question: A building-shaped solid consists of a 10×8×4 rectangular prism and a triangular-prism roof whose triangular cross section has base 10 and height 3 and whose length is 8. Find the total volume.
solution: Body volume=10·8·4=320. Roof volume=(1/2)·10·3·8=120. Total=440 cubic units.

question: Two rectangular prisms overlap. Prism A is 7×4×3; prism B is 3×4×5. Their overlap is exactly a 3×4×3 prism. Find the volume of their union.
solution: Add both full volumes and subtract the overlap once: 7·4·3+3·4·5−3·4·3=84+60−36=108.
